## Why

WV-10 (ADR-188, ratified 2026-10-01) waived INGEST-035's
no-direct-capture clause for Flock transparency portals ONLY: "SIG may
fetch Flock portal pages only when served without a challenge, and stops
on any challenge." The waiver exists so the portals' *aggregates* — the
counts/config/sharing fields the transparency pages publish — can be
probed lawfully once the operator runs P36.12's Wave-B leg. This ticket
lands the machinery and the evidence surface; it performs no probe.

## What ships

- **`connectors/flock_portal_probe.py`** — the `flock_portal_probe`
  connector (eight-stage, sibling of `flock_portal.py`). One polite GET
  per committed portal per run through `ctx.fetcher` only — the shared
  `PoliteFetcher` runs the opt-out register, robots probing (recorded,
  never silently bypassed), rate limiting and the challenge boundary.
  Served-page order: **mirror-schema parse** (the portal's embedded JSON
  island read against the mirror's own aggregate-only vocabulary;
  denied-field names recorded, values never read) → **reconcile**
  (existence + §29.3 configured-sharing edges through P08.2's reconciler)
  → **in-memory Part VIII screen** over the embedded payload AND the
  canonical extraction, before any persistence (`ScreenedRefusal`, counts
  only) → **verbatim terms capture** → **CC BY-SA 4.0 `portal`
  compartment stamping**. Persisted bytes: `sig.flock-portal-page/1` —
  the screened extraction, never the vendor's raw HTML (§8.4 DERIVE).
  No retry, no circumvention capability, no credentials, no crawler.
- **Committed probe set** — `data/flock_portal_probe_targets.toml`
  (`sig.flock-portal-probe-targets/1`): the 917 known portals from the
  Eyes on Flock aggregator inventory snapshot (2026-09-23T10:15:16.751Z,
  sha256 `eccb336a…` recorded; capture log path recorded), selection rule
  = non-empty `organizations_shared_with` (I3-L005), slug-sorted,
  `{slug, url}` rows only. `discover()` refuses targets outside the set —
  ADR-188 adds no discovery method.
- **`sig.probe-run/1`** — `probe_run_record()` builds exactly one record
  per run: per-portal `served`/`refused`/`deferred`/`resumed`/
  `not_attempted` outcomes with the refusal kind (`challenge`,
  `interstitial`, `opt_out`, `PortalOptedOut`, `rights_reservation`,
  `schema_refusal`, `screened`, `http_*`, `unreachable`), inventory
  provenance, deduplicated verbatim terms, checks block (coverage /
  served / refusals / part-viii-screen / compartment), and an output
  digest. An all-refused run is a **pass** (expected yield ≈ 0 is honest);
  a run that attempted nothing — or whose outcome ledger disagrees with
  the driver's fetch count — is a **fail**. Live runs write it under
  `capture_dir/probe_records/` (the hook fires only when the gated row
  is later flipped).
- **Shared infra** — `evidence.screen.declaration_from_table` (the
  TOML→`ScreenDeclaration` parser moved beside the engine; the probe
  parses the SAME committed `ops/at_rest_audit.toml` document — no
  drifted copy; `ops.at_rest_audit` delegates), `stages.py` gains
  `SchemaRefusal` + `ScreenedRefusal`, recorded by the pipeline like the
  P36.1a rights refusals.
- **Registry** — `flock_transparency_portals` (the pre-existing vendor
  row — one source, one row): custody `LINK` → `DERIVE` (only the
  screened aggregate extraction persists), `access_method` records the
  WV-10 probe envelope, `notes` + `rights.publication_basis` carry the
  WV-10/D3-Q3=b basis verbatim, `robots_policy="honor"`,
  **`ingestion_permitted` stays absent (false)**. The `link_only`
  disposition row was removed (one-disposition invariant — a
  connector-mapped source's disposition is "live via connector").
  `live_targets.toml` maps it via `flock_portal_probe_targets` → the
  committed inventory. `CONNECTOR_FOR_SOURCE` routes it to
  `flock_portal_probe`. `eyes_on_flock` is byte-for-byte untouched.
- **Tests** — `tests/connectors/test_flock_portal_probe.py` (28) +
  fixtures (`served_sunnydale.html`, `served_hellmouth_screened.html`,
  `served_terms_payload.html`, `interstitial.html`, `no_payload.html`,
  `slug_mismatch.html`, `challenge_403.html`). Zero network.

- `uv run pytest tests/connectors/test_flock_portal_probe.py` — **28
  passed** (0.4s; full matrix in `docs/build/runs/P36.74.md`).
- `sig-connectors validate` — green; `gate --source
  flock_transparency_portals` → **REFUSED** (fail-closed pre-flip).
- `make check` — lint/format/mypy/pytest: green except the pre-existing

  `vars.SIG_GCP_PROJECT`; unrelated to this diff).
- Demonstrable screen: a fixture page carrying `search_audit[].plate` is
  refused WHOLE (`PUB002-PLATES` hit), zero bytes persisted; the served
  fixture's denied `description` field is recorded by name only.

## Deviations / deferrals

- **Existing row reused** (not a duplicate `flock_portal_probe` row) —
  the registry's `flock_transparency_portals` IS the vendor source;
  custody moved `LINK` → `DERIVE` matching what the connector persists.
- **Persisted artifact is the screened extraction, not raw HTML** — the
  ADR-185-honest form (the screen's rules run over field structure); raw
  bytes are fetched once, screened, dropped.
- **Screen refuses whole pages** carrying any screen-vocab field —
  "a flagged page is refused whole", and it makes the in-memory gate
  demonstrable.
- The upstream snapshot log is gitignored (`docs/build/logs/`); its
  sha256/date/selection rule are committed in the inventory and the
  derivation is recorded — reproducible, not re-fetched.
- No new deferrals; no human gates ticked; no live fetch attempted.
